The Buggy Technician is responsible for the inspection, maintenance, troubleshooting, and repair of electric and gasoline-powered buggies/golf carts used in operations, hospitality, events, resorts, airports, or industrial facilities.
Perform preventive maintenance on buggies/golf carts.
Diagnose electrical, mechanical, and hydraulic faults.
Repair batteries, motors, controllers, brakes, steering, suspension, and lighting systems.
Conduct routine inspections and safety checks.
Maintain charging systems and battery health.
Keep maintenance records and service reports updated.
Ensure vehicles are clean, operational, and available for daily use.
Respond quickly to breakdowns and emergency repair requests.
Follow workplace safety and manufacturer guidelines.
q: Diploma/ITI in Mechanical or Electrical Engineering preferred.
Experience in golf cart, buggy, or small vehicle maintenance.
Knowledge of electric vehicle systems and battery troubleshooting.
Ability to use diagnostic tools and repair equipment.
Basic understanding of wiring diagrams and technical manuals.

d: Right now, thousands of people in the UAE book a cleaner through Justlife and expect them to show up on time, do excellent work, and leave their home better than they found it. That promise only holds if the cleaners are there, trained, motivated, and routed efficiently — which means someone has to own the daily operating reality of that supply chain: keeping cleaners deployed, partners accountable, costs disciplined, and quality high.

This is an operations role, not a strategy role. You'll run the DTC home cleaning business end-to-end — 300+ cleaners across multiple partner companies, a small on-ground team of account executives and roster agents, and measurable improvement in on-time performance, completion rates, and contribution margin within your first six months. Every day you'll make decisions that move the numbers: which partner hires next, how to incentivise productivity, where fuel and routing waste money, whether we're hitting our supply plan. This is what it means to own a real business line.
You'll love this role if you...
You think in unit economics and get frustrated when a cost lever stays hidden in a spreadsheet instead of being fixed
You've run a large field or blue-collar workforce (directly or through partners) and know exactly how to hold external teams accountable without being their boss
You're energised by problems you can see and touch — you'd rather spend an hour in a van or at a partner accommodation than sit in a meeting
You build teams that work without you, and you actively coach people into bigger roles
You obsess over data quality because you know bad reports kill decisions, and you'll learn SQL or Power BI yourself rather than wait for someone to build your dashboard

Drive sustained improvement in on-time %, completion rate %, promise-kept %, and absent rate % by building daily operating discipline — reviewing metrics with the team each morning, identifying blockers, and acting on them before they compound into service failures

Lead and develop the on-ground operations team (2 account executives and 4 remote roster agents): set clear priorities, review performance daily, coach individuals toward higher capability, and manage accountability

Own supply planning and growth: forecast cleaner headcount needed against demand by city and partner, manage onboarding pace and allocation across partner companies, and reduce time-to-deployment so new hires contribute faster

Manage partner companies as senior counterparts: run monthly business reviews, hold them to service-level agreements and commercial terms, reconcile statements of account with finance monthly, and escalate issues before they become crises

Design and drive cost and process projects that improve contribution margin — incentive structure redesigns, fuel and fleet controls, van routing optimisation, cleaner orientation and training — taking each from idea to measurable result

Build and maintain reporting that surfaces what's driving performance: which partners are slipping, where attrition is highest, which cost levers moved margin, what's blocking supply. Act on what it shows
Spend meaningful time in the field — in vans, accommodations, and partner sites — so you understand problems first-hand and your team sees you do the same
What tells us you're the one

You've measurably improved operational metrics across a large field workforce — tell us a specific program you ran (incentive redesign, routing optimisation, vendor onboarding, training rollout, etc.) and the metric that moved as a result: completion rate up X%, on-time performance improved Y%, attrition fell Z%, or margin lifted by N%

You can spot cause and effect: when a metric moves, you know whether it's partner execution, process design, incentive misalignment, or something else — and you know how to test your hypothesis before rolling out a fix

You've managed blue-collar, field-based, or logistics workforces (home services, facilities management, staffing, last-mile delivery, quick commerce) — or run marketplace operations where supply quality depends on external partners. Results matter far more than years, but 5–7 years of this kind of work is the sweet spot
You're fluent in data: you can build operating reports independently, interrogate a spreadsheet without help, and use SQL, Power BI, or AI tools to automate manual reporting so you have time to think

You speak fluent English, written and spoken. Bonus: you speak languages common to the workforce in the UAE (Tagalog, Urdu, Arabic), or you have prior experience operating in the UAE market in home services, logistics, or staffing

Scale and impact: You'll run a real, revenue-generating business line serving thousands of customers across the UAE, managing hundreds of cleaners and multiple partner companies, with direct line of sight from your decisions to customer satisfaction and margin
Clear growth path: this role is a launchpad into broader category leadership, multi-city operations, or general management as we scale across the GCC
Close partnership with leadership: you'll work alongside the Business Development lead and the founding team, with real influence on strategy and resource decisions
A fair, performance-driven culture: you'll be measured on the metrics you own, recognised through our JustHeroes program, and rewarded for results — not politics
Startup benefits: a birthday day off (JustHoliday), free Justlife service credits, referral bonuses, and regular team experiences
Join the tribe and let's become #everydaybetter, together.

The primary responsibility of a Care Advisor is to handle telephone inquiries related to the company’s products and services, adhering to established scripts and procedures. The role requires ensuring that all calls are answered within defined service levels while maintaining the highest standards of customer service excellence. In addition, the Care Advisor is responsible for accurately documenting details of each interaction, including actions taken, to facilitate follow-ups and any necessary corrective measures. The role also involves maintaining effective communication with the Care Centre Team Leader and Assistant Manager, while consistently delivering a customer-focused service experience.
q: 0 -2 years experience in a Call Centre/ Customer Service environment, TPA Hospitals or Medical Centers exposure a plus.
Strong communication skills in English (additional languages are an advantage)
Good understanding of customer service principles and telephone etiquette
Physically fit to carry out duties.
Legally permitted to work in the country of operations.
Fluency in MS Office (Excel, Word, Outlook, PowerPoint) and general internet navigation and research skills.
